title: Dutch AI extension category
description: One category file: its own bilingual title plus one listing per artifact. Every field is required; no optional fields in v1.

title.description: The category's display title. Lives here, not in the filename — the filename is only a stable slug, so a title can be reworded without renaming the file.

nl.description: Dutch mirror of the English title, in Dutch sentence case.

id.description: Stable slug; join key for every surface and later usage events.

description_nl.description: Dutch mirror of description_en: one outcome-first sentence, same register. Product/vendor names stay untranslated.

target.description: Ids from data/targets.json of the Dutch service, data source, standard, or authority this integration lets an agent reach or work with; the outcome axis listings are grouped and searched by.

type.description: The outermost unit the publisher ships — how you install it, not what it can do. See `bundles` for what is inside.

bundles.description: What this install unit contains, so the capabilities inside a single row stay findable. All four arrays are required; empty means none of that kind. A one-artifact listing bundles nothing — the row *is* the artifact — so all four are empty. For a large multi-jurisdiction bundle, list only the Dutch-relevant entries.

skills.description: Skill names as the publisher ships them — the directory holding each SKILL.md. Shared-resource pseudo-skills (`_shared`) are infrastructure, not capabilities; leave them out.

commands.description: Slash-command names without the leading slash — the basename of each file in `commands/`.

agents.description: Subagent names — the basename of each file in `agents/`.

mcp_servers.description: Keys from the bundled `mcpServers` config that serve the listing's purpose. The publisher's own ops plumbing (monitoring, admin backends) is not a bundled capability; leave it out.
